entity.name: Areeb Ahmed
entity.description: Independent developer and final-year computer science student in India. I build and maintain Airhop on my own, in the open, under the MIT license.

projects.name: Airhop
projects.description: Airhop is a private messaging app for Android, iOS, desktop, smartwatches and CLI that works with no internet, no accounts and no central servers. Messages relay directly between devices over a Bluetooth Low Energy mesh, so people stay in contact when the network is unavailable, saturated, surveilled or shut down. It is wire-compatible with bitchat, so devices running either app join the same mesh with zero setup. Identity is an Ed25519 key pair held only on the device, live sessions use the Noise XX handshake with Double Ratchet forward secrecy, and Nostr relays, optionally over Tor, carry traffic when a connection is available. It also carries offline Cashu ecash payments that settle between two devices with no internet on either side.

plans.name: Device lab
plans.description: A few used low-end Android handsets and a pair of ESP32 boards with 915 MHz LoRa radios, since Bluetooth discovery, background execution and OEM battery managers can only be tested on real hardware.

plans.name: External review of the cryptography
plans.description: An independent review of the Noise XX handshake and Double Ratchet implementation, with the findings published. A first step toward the full audit, which costs far more.

history.description: No grants, investment or institutional funding received to date. Developer accounts, test devices and hosting have been paid for personally.
